data.name: SuperTrucks Offroad Racing
data.detailed_description:
Inspired by the arcade/NES classic racing game - Super Offroad, SuperTrucks Offroad Racing brings you a modern take on the beloved classic.

TOUGH OFF ROAD RACING CONDITIONS
Race off road in conditions such as sand, mud, snow and tarmac, giving you plenty of racing variety.

CUSTOMISE YOUR TRUCK
Pimp your ride with a selection of paints, decals and tyre sets ranging from common to legendary!
Unlock more cosmetic items for your truck as you progress in the game and collect crates...

UPGRADE
The racing action starts off slow but as you upgrade, things get faster...
The further you progress, the faster the AI will become and the better your drifting and management of nitro will need to be.

Upgrade your ENGINE, EXHAUST, TYRES, SUSPENSION and NITRO to best suit your racing style!

SEMI-REALISTIC RACING
The driving model is semi-realistic and drifting around corners using nitro at the right time is the key to good racing.

AERIAL CONTROL
In the 2.3 update, we have added aerial control, allowing you to do backips and 360 spins while hitting those big airs.

OVERHAULED AI
In the 2.3 update, we have completely overhauled the AI system, the AI is now challenging more than ever.

CONTROLLER SUPPORT IN-RACE
Racing with a controller is supported in-race only. Key bindings can be set in Settings.
We will be releasing a brand new, overhauled UI for the game in the next 2.4 update, which will provide full controller menu support.

CAREER MODE
Race in 7 cities across the US, with each city having its own challenging boss to beat.
Unlock hardcore mode once you've beaten all 7 race bosses.

DAILY LEADERBOARD EVENTS
Enter the Long Jump, Time Trial and Obstacle Course events.
Cosmetic items and currency are granted to each player who finishes in the Top 5 positions daily.

reviews.review:
Purchased this game as I was a huge fan of the original Ivan "Ironman" Stewart's Super Off-Road Arcade game. After having played it, there is little in common with the original style or gameplay. Namely: 

1) Racing feels slow and kludgy. 

2) Controls lack precision. Very easy to spin out and lose races. It feels like you're steering the Griswold's 1979 Ford LTD Country Squire Station Wagon - you have to turn the wheel a full rotation just to make the tires turn a little bit. Driving on a track feels more like snowboarding down a slope. 

3) Upgrades don't make sense (there are several categories, such as exhaust, engine, etc). There are only limited slots you can use - but many categories of items that can fill these limited slots. No explanation whether a muffler or exhaust manifold (for example) would be better in those slots, nor any performance explanation after you fill the slots with different components. (For tires, one of the items is tire bolts. Does this mean I'm driving around without tire bolts without this upgrade?)

4) Nitro isn't like original, where you push it and get a nitro blast. It's more like a nitro squirt gun, where you hold the button down and as you hold it the truck goes faster. (This was a big dissapointment, as one of my fondest memories of the original arcade game was banging on the nitro button, getting enough nitro blasts to win a race) 

5) Sound effects are weak. You can acquire certain prizes during the race (such as a wrench, which lowers damage, or a money bag which increases your coin by an unknown amount) - but the sound effects are so soft that when you hit the icon, you can't tell if you even got the added bonus or not 

6) Boring chellenges. Example: A bunch of concrete barriers are laid out in a pattern. You need to drive your way through the maze in a certain time. If you don't achieve the goal, the goal is made easier automatically. (Adds more time for you). 

7) Graphics, UI and ambiance feel like something out of the late 90s. It reminds me a lot of San Francisco Rush on the N64 (only graphically, sans the fun gameplay). 

8) Must use a combination of Xbox remote and keyboard. There is no way to just use the Xbox remote to navigate through menus, etc. (If there is, it is not easy to figure out, and the game will make you program your remote prior to working in the menus). 

I really wanted to get into this game, and I tried, to no avail. Unfortunately cannot recommend this game. Although it was inspired by Ivan "Ironman" Stewart's Super Off-Road, there is zero likeness to it other than the fact that it has trucks in it.
